messages.subject: [REMINDER] Airflow Contributor Day in Glasgow
messages.body:
Hello Everyone,

This is a short reminder for those who may have forgotten: we have
"Airflow Contributor Day" as part of the Apache Software Foundation's
"Community Over Code Glasgow 2026" event, starting this weekend. There
is still time to register.

We will have a number of contributors there, along with some surprises
and unexpected guests ;) - you will find out what I mean when it
starts.

There are some fantastic talks prepared. Airflow Contributor Day is
going to happen on Sunday 11th of October. If you do not want to spend
4 days in Glasgow, you could certainly come just for Sunday (but it's
a great opportunity to meet and mingle and listen to other ASF
projects).

Also, the day before—Saturday, 10th of October—is Lakehouse Day, which
will likely be very interesting for many active contributors. This
might be a nice weekend gathering :).

The talks for the Airflow Contributor Day:

* Pavan Kumar: Agentic Operators in Apache Airflow: Reliable,
Observable, Human-Governed AI
* Shahar Epstein:  Bringing AI to Airflow: Community, Design, and Trust
* Vincent Beck: Event-driven scheduling in Airflow: What's next?
* Ping Zangh, Hongyi Wang: Re-architecting Airflow at OpenAI: Scaling
to 70K+ Tasks in 6 Weeks with Codex
* Jason Liu, Wei-Lee: Airflow Beyond Python: New Languages for Tasks
and Workflows
* Amogh Desai: The evolution of durable execution in Airflow
* David Blein: Apache Airflow: from await to iterate

Detailed schedule in [3].

J.


[1] Airlflow Contributor Day -
https://communityovercode.apache.org/events/glasgow-2026/airflow-contributor-day-glasgow
[2] Lakehouse Day -
https://communityovercode.apache.org/events/glasgow-2026/lakehouse-day-glasgow
[3] Schedule: https://web.cvent.com/event/ac71ce47-2b5f-424c-abfe-5b48255315fb/summary?RefId=XSummary
(filter by Airflow Contributor Day)

messages.subject: Re: [REMINDER] Airflow Contributor Day in Glasgow
messages.body:
Hi Jarek,

Thanks for the reminder! 

+ Amogh so we can coordinate our talks.

1. BTW I don't see our accepted talk being included in the Airflow filter when filtering the schedule by Airflow Contributor Day. Should it be included in that track?

Disruption-Ready Airflow: Resumable Operators and Infra Retry Budgets for Kubernetes at Scale <https://web.cvent.com/event/ac71ce47-2b5f-424c-abfe-5b48255315fb/summary?session=4ee58356-f528-4989-8b0b-2c7f57d8c415&shareLink=true>
2. Amogh, sorry for the seemlingly-overlap with your talk, The evolution of durable execution in Airflow <https://web.cvent.com/event/ac71ce47-2b5f-424c-abfe-5b48255315fb/summary?session=9b3a0f3f-bf8a-45e3-9ee8-8bca236bfa09&shareLink=true>. When we submitted our proposal, AIP-96 was still there (or I might have missed). AIP-103 has since superseded it, but our title still reflects the earlier scope - will email the organizer to update ours to drop that scope, or if Jarek / some other committer / PMC has access, we can come up an updated name together and update it directly (Maybe Disruption-Ready Airflow: Infrastructure Recovery and Kubernetes Migration?). Will make sure to keep the AIP-103 and resumable-operator walkthrough out of our talk and point attendees to yours for that material.

Our talk will focus on:

Keeping workflows running through Kubernetes infrastructure failures. Our internal recovery mechanisms already support thousands of task instances each day, helping interrupted tasks recover while preserving users' retry budgets for application failures. We'll explain how pod watches and state reconciliation support that recovery, and connect our operational experience to AIP-97 failure classification and AIP-122 infrastructure retries
Moving Airflow between Kubernetes clusters while long-running workflows continue, without a global service shutdown. We'll share how we managed execution ownership, worker-pod reconciliation, and a gradual cutover in production.
We'd be glad to coordinate examples so attendees get two complementary perspectives.

AIP-97: https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=399279312
AIP-122: https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=451974654

Best,
Stefan

messages.subject: Re: [REMINDER] Airflow Contributor Day in Glasgow
messages.body:
Thanks, Jarek and Amogh

Looks like for our talk we'll keep our Monday slot.

We are aligned that the resumable operators and AIP-103 is for Amogh's talk. 

The other one will instead focus on infrastructure recovery and AIP-97/122 (introduced again and discussed briefly in October 8 this morning’s dev call), plus migrating Airflow between Kubernetes clusters without a global shutdown. I'll try to ask the organizers to update the title to reflect that scope, if they don’t get to it in time, at least internally within Airflow this should resolve it.

Looking forward to meeting everyone in Glasgow! It'll be my first visit to the UK, and I'm really excited.

Best,

Stefan
